I'm building real Steam Workshop integration for 11 game families: ark, unturned, dst, squad, empyrion, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2, icarus, palworld. I need exact facts extracted from the code, not summaries — quote exact field names, exact object literals, exact line numbers.

Read these files IN FULL and report back:

1. `/opt/nxeon/lib/game-control.ts` — the `GAME_CONTROL` record. For each of the 11 families above (their exact keys in this file — they may be named slightly differently, e.g. "projectzomboid" vs "pz"), report the FULL object: data root path, any existing appid field, RCON/config info, any existing workshop/mod-id config field, container/docker image reference, and anything about how the server process is launched (command line args if present). Quote verbatim.

2. `/opt/nxeon/lib/game-config.ts` — for the same 11 families, find and quote every config KEY related to workshop/mods (things like GAME_MOD_IDS, ModIds, MODS, workshop_collection, KF2_SERVER_SUBSCRIBED_WORKSHOP_ITEMS etc — I saw some via grep already) — quote the full object literal for each key found (key, label, group, type, default, phase, help), and identify which env var / config line it maps to when the server is deployed (look for where GAME_CONFIGS or similar is consumed, e.g. in worker or deploy scripts, to see the real mapping from this config key to an actual file/env var written to the VM).

3. `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts` — full contents. This is likely the server action backing the "Add to my server" button for GameMod. Quote it in full or near-full (up to ~350 lines, feasible).

4. `/opt/nxeon/prisma/seed-gamemods.ts` — full contents (267 lines). It already has a `steam_workshop` case building a URL from an id. Quote the surrounding function and any per-source logic.

5. `/opt/nxeon/lib/mods-catalog.ts` — full contents (431 lines), especially anything about `steam_workshop` label/rendering, and the shape of a catalog "mod" object used by the UI (fields it expects).

6. Also check `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx` (I saw `steam_workshop: "Steam Workshop"` there around line 40) — read enough context (100 lines around it) to see how the UI renders a Steam Workshop badge and whether there's already an "Add to my server" button/flow referencing sourceId for steam_workshop items.

7. Check `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma` for the `ServerMod` model (fields), and the `Server` model's fields relevant to config writing (look for something like `dataRoot`, `configPath`, `gameVariant`, or a JSON config blob field) — just enough to know how a server's "desired config" is currently stored/applied.

8. Check whether there's an existing "GAME_CONFIG_SYNC" or "game-config" worker job (likely `worker/game-config.ts` or similar) that writes config KV pairs to a live VM — read it in full if under 500 lines, otherwise read the first 200 lines and grep for how it writes files (look for `writeFile`, `sftp`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `ServerConfig` model reads). I need to understand precisely how a config key (like GAME_MOD_IDS) that already exists in game-config.ts actually gets turned into bytes on the VM's disk (e.g. an .ini file line, a docker env var, a command line arg) — this is critical since I'll be reusing this exact same mechanism to write Workshop IDs.

9. Search for any existing `appid` references for these 11 families anywhere in the repo (steamcmd install scripts, provisioning, `scripts/`, `lib/provision*`) — e.g. grep -rn "app_update\|appid\|APPID" across lib/ scripts/ worker/ for ark, unturned, dst (App ID 343050), squad, empyrion, soulmask, projectzomboid (380870), tf2 (440), l4d2 (550), icarus, palworld — report every real numeric Steam AppID you find referenced in this codebase for each family, verbatim with file:line.

Report back concisely but completely — this is feeding directly into code I'm about to write, so precision on field names/types matters far more than prose. Include file:line citations for everything.

1	/**
2	 * Game server control panel — SSH/RCON transport + per-family control facts.
3	 *
4	 * A plain server-side module (NO "use server", no client imports). Imported by
5	 * BOTH the server actions (lib/actions-game-control.ts) and the worker
6	 * (worker/game-control.ts). It NEVER runs in the browser — the customer's root
7	 * credentials and their server's RCON password stay on our server.
8	 *
9	 * Everything here operates on the CUSTOMER'S OWN game VM over the platform's
10	 * existing SSH (host/port/root-password derived exactly like lib/sftp.ts, reused
11	 * via lib/ssh-exec.ts `withServerSsh`). Two transport rules, mirroring the rest of
12	 * the control panel:
13	 *
14	 *   1. STRICT ALLOWLIST VALIDATION for anything that reaches a shell. Ports, unit
15	 *      names, paths and file names are validated/allowlisted or rejected — never
16	 *      sanitized. Family/unit hints are compile-time constants, never customer
17	 *      input.
18	 *
19	 *   2. RCON never touches a shell at all. We read the server's RCON port/password
20	 *      out of its own config file, then open a TCP channel to 127.0.0.1:<port> on
21	 *      the game VM THROUGH the SSH connection (`conn.forwardOut`) and speak the
22	 *      Source RCON wire protocol directly. The RCON port is never exposed off the
23	 *      box, the password is only ever a protocol packet body (not an argv token),
24	 *      and the customer's console command is validated to be single-line/control-
25	 *      char-free before it is sent.
26	 *
27	 * SANDBOX: callers gate real SSH behind `!SANDBOX`; on staging the inline reads
28	 * return realistic synthetic data so the whole UX works without a live VM.
29	 */
30	import type { Duplex } from "node:stream";
31	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
32	import { GAME_FAMILIES, type GameFamily } from "./games";
33	import { exec, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS } from "./ssh-exec";
34	
35	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
36	// Per-family control facts
37	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	
39	/** How (if at all) we can talk to a running server's console remotely. */
40	export type RconProtocol =
41	  | "source" // Valve Source RCON (Minecraft, CS2, Palworld) — implemented here
42	  | "rust-web" // Rust WebSocket RCON — different protocol, deferred
43	  | "none"; // no remote console protocol (Valheim/Terraria vanilla)
44	
45	/** Where a family stores the RCON credentials, and how to parse that file. */
46	type RconConfig = {
47	  /** Config-file path candidates to try first (absolute). */
48	  candidates: string[];
49	  /** Roots to bounded-`find` under if none of the candidates exist. */
50	  findRoots: string[];
51	  /** File name to find. */
52	  findName: string;
53	  /** File format. */
54	  kind: "properties" | "palworld-ini";
55	  /** Key that gates RCON being on (value compared case-insensitively to true/1). */
56	  enableKey?: string;
57	  /** Key holding the RCON password. */
58	  passwordKey: string;
59	  /** Key holding the RCON port (falls back to `defaultPort`). */
60	  portKey?: string;
61	  /** Port used when the file does not specify one. */
62	  defaultPort: number;
63	};
64	
65	export type GameControlSpec = {
66	  family: GameFamily;
67	  label: string;
68	  /** systemd unit-name hints (first that resolves wins). Compile-time constants. */
69	  serviceHints: string[];
70	  /** Directory candidates that hold the world/save data (for listing + backup). */
71	  dataRoots: string[];
72	  /** Remote console protocol. */
73	  rcon: RconProtocol;
74	  /** Where/how to read RCON creds (present only when rcon === "source"). */
75	  rconConfig?: RconConfig;
76	  /** RCON verb that lists connected players (present when supported). */
77	  listCommand?: string;
78	  /** RCON verb template for kicking a player (`%s` = validated name/id). */
79	  kickCommand?: string;
80	  /** RCON verb template for banning a player (`%s` = validated name/id). */
81	  banCommand?: string;
82	};
83	
84	/**
85	 * The control facts per game family.
86	 *
87	 * RCON reality (why not every "has RCON" game gets a wire here):
88	 *  - minecraft: native Source RCON (enable-rcon / rcon.password / rcon.port).
89	 *  - cs2:       native Source RCON (rcon_password; port defaults to the game port).
90	 *  - palworld:  native RCON, Source-protocol framing (RCONEnabled/RCONPort/AdminPassword).
91	 *  - rust:      RCON is WebSocket (rcon.web) — a DIFFERENT protocol; deferred.
92	 *  - valheim:   no native RCON (needs a BepInEx mod) — console disabled.
93	 *  - terraria:  vanilla has only a local stdin console — console disabled.
94	 */
95	export const GAME_CONTROL: Record<GameFamily, GameControlSpec> = {
96	  minecraft: {
97	    family: "minecraft",
98	    label: "Minecraft",
99	    serviceHints: ["minecraft", "minecraft-server"],
100	    // `/opt/mc` is first because it's the actual host bind-mount the paid
101	    // template's setup script uses (`-v /opt/mc:/data`, prisma/catalog.ts) —
102	    // without it here, world listing silently found nothing while RCON

409	/**
410	 * Locate the first existing file: explicit candidates via `test -f`, then a
411	 * bounded `find` over `roots`. Candidate paths are compile-time constants; the
412	 * returned hit is re-validated against the path allowlist before any caller uses
413	 * it. Returns null when nothing matches.
414	 */
415	export async function remoteLocateFile(
416	  conn: Client,
417	  candidates: string[],
418	  roots: string[],
419	  name: string
420	): Promise<string | null> {
421	  const testExpr = candidates.map((p) => `if [ -f ${shq(p)} ]; then echo ${shq(p)}; exit 0; fi;`).join(" ");
422	  const findExpr = roots.length
423	    ? `for r in ${roots.map((r) => shq(r)).join(" ")}; do [ -d "$r" ] && find "$r" -maxdepth 6 -type f -name ${shq(name)} 2>/dev/null | head -1; done | head -1`
424	    : "true";
425	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, `${testExpr} ${findExpr}`, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
426	  const hit = stdout
427	    .split(/\r?\n/)
428	    .map((s) => s.trim())
429	    .find((s) => s.length > 0);
430	  return hit && isSafeRemotePath(hit) ? hit : null;
431	}

452	/** Parse a `key=value` / `key value` config into a lowercase-keyed map. */
453	function parseFlatConfig(text: string): Record<string, string> {
454	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
455	  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
456	    const t = line.trim();
457	    if (!t || t.startsWith("#") || t.startsWith("//") || t.startsWith("!") || t.startsWith(";")) continue;
458	    let key: string;
459	    let val: string;
460	    const eq = t.indexOf("=");
461	    if (eq >= 0) {
462	      key = t.slice(0, eq).trim();
463	      val = t.slice(eq + 1).trim();
464	    } else {
465	      const sp = t.search(/\s/);
466	      if (sp < 0) continue;
467	      key = t.slice(0, sp).trim();
468	      val = t.slice(sp + 1).trim();
469	    }
470	    // Strip surrounding quotes.
471	    val = val.replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1").replace(/^'(.*)'$/, "$1");
472	    if (key) out[key.toLowerCase()] = val;
473	  }
474	  return out;
475	}

479	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
480	  const idx = text.indexOf("OptionSettings=(");
481	  const open = idx >= 0 ? text.indexOf("(", idx) : -1;
482	  const close = open >= 0 ? text.indexOf(")", open) : -1;
483	  if (open < 0 || close < 0) return out;
484	  const inner = text.slice(open + 1, close);
485	  let cur = "";
486	  let inQuote = false;
487	  const pairs: string[] = [];
488	  for (const ch of inner) {
489	    if (ch === '"') inQuote = !inQuote;

546	const RCON_TYPE_AUTH = 3;
547	const RCON_TYPE_EXEC = 2;
548	const RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE = 0;

550	const RCON_ID_CMD = 0x2;
551	const RCON_ID_END = 0x2711; // sentinel id for the trailing empty packet

553	function rconPacket(id: number, type: number, body: string): Buffer {
554	  const bodyBuf = Buffer.from(body, "ascii");
555	  const buf = Buffer.alloc(bodyBuf.length + 14);
556	  buf.writeInt32LE(bodyBuf.length + 10, 0); // size = id(4)+type(4)+body+2 nulls
557	  buf.writeInt32LE(id, 4);
558	  buf.writeInt32LE(type, 8);
559	  bodyBuf.copy(buf, 12);
560	  // two trailing NUL bytes already zero from Buffer.alloc
561	  return buf;

564	/**
565	 * Open a TCP channel to `host:port` on the game VM THROUGH the authenticated SSH
566	 * connection. The RCON port therefore never needs to be reachable off the box.
567	 */
568	export function forwardTcp(conn: Client, host: string, port: number, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<Duplex> {
569	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
570	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("Timed out opening RCON channel")), timeoutMs);
571	    conn.forwardOut("127.0.0.1", 0, host, port, (err, stream) => {
572	      clearTimeout(timer);
573	      if (err) return reject(err);
574	      resolve(stream as unknown as Duplex);
575	    });
576	  });

579	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };

581	/**
582	 * Speak Source RCON over `stream`: authenticate, run `command`, and read the
583	 * (possibly multi-packet) response, using a trailing empty packet as the
584	 * end-of-response sentinel. Never throws — resolves an {ok,error} result. The
585	 * password is only ever a packet body; the command was validated by the caller.
586	 */
587	export function sourceRcon(stream: Duplex, password: string, command: string, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<RconResult> {
588	  return new Promise((resolve) => {
589	    let acc = Buffer.alloc(0);
590	    let authed = false;
591	    let response = "";
592	    let done = false;
593	
594	    const finish = (r: RconResult) => {
595	      if (done) return;
596	      done = true;
597	      clearTimeout(timer);
598	      try {
599	        stream.end();
600	      } catch {
601	        /* best effort */
602	      }
603	      resolve(r);
604	    };
605	    const timer = setTimeout(
606	      () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON timed out (no response)." }),
607	      timeoutMs
608	    );
609	
610	    stream.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => {
611	      acc = Buffer.concat([acc, chunk]);
612	      while (acc.length >= 4) {
613	        const size = acc.readInt32LE(0);
614	        if (size < 10 || size > 4110) return finish({ ok: false, error: "Malformed RCON response." });
615	        if (acc.length < size + 4) break;
616	        const id = acc.readInt32LE(4);
617	        const type = acc.readInt32LE(8);
618	        const body = acc.slice(12, 4 + size - 2).toString("ascii");
619	        acc = acc.slice(4 + size);
620	
621	        if (!authed) {
622	          // The auth response is a type-2 (AUTH_RESPONSE) packet; id === -1 on failure.
623	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_EXEC) {
624	            if (id === -1) return finish({ ok: false, error: "RCON authentication failed (wrong password)." });
625	            authed = true;
626	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_CMD, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, command));
627	            stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_END, RCON_TYPE_EXEC, "")); // sentinel
628	          }
629	          // A leading empty RESPONSE_VALUE some servers send pre-auth is ignored.
630	        } else {
631	          if (id === RCON_ID_END) return finish({ ok: true, response });
632	          if (type === RCON_TYPE_RESPONSE) response += body;
633	        }
634	      }
635	    });
636	    stream.on("error", (e: Error) => finish({ ok: false, error: e?.message || "RCON connection error." }));
637	    stream.on("close", () => finish(authed ? { ok: true, response } : { ok: false, error: "RCON connection closed." }));
638	
639	    stream.write(rconPacket(RCON_ID_AUTH, RCON_TYPE_AUTH, password));
640	  });

647	 */
648	export async function runRcon(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, command: string): Promise<RconResult> {
649	  const creds = await readRconCreds(conn, spec);
650	  if (!creds.ok) return { ok: false, error: creds.reason };
651	  let stream: Duplex;
652	  try {
653	    stream = await forwardTcp(conn, "127.0.0.1", creds.port);
654	  } catch (e) {
655	    return { ok: false, error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not open RCON channel." };

671	 * (compile-time constants), then reads the last `n` journal lines; if journald has
672	 * nothing, falls back to a `.log` file under the data roots. Read-only.
673	 */
674	export async function readGameLogs(conn: Client, spec: GameControlSpec, n = 200): Promise<LogResult> {
675	  const lines = Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(n) || 200, 20), 500);
676	  const hints = spec.serviceHints.map(shq).join(" ");
677	  const roots = spec.dataRoots.map(shq).join(" ");
678	  const script = [
679	    `unit=""`,
680	    `for c in ${hints}; do systemctl cat "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { unit="$c"; break; }; done`,
681	    `if [ -z "$unit" ]; then unit=$(systemctl list-units --type=service --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i ${shq(spec.family)} | head -1 | awk '{print $1}'); fi`,
682	    `echo "NXLOG:UNIT:${"$"}{unit:-none}"`,
683	    `if [ -n "$unit" ]; then journalctl -u "$unit" -n ${lines} --no-pager 2>/dev/null; fi`,
684	    // Fallback: newest *.log under the data roots (bounded).
685	    `f=""; for r in ${roots}; do [ -d "$r" ] && f=$(find "$r" -maxdepth 4 -type f -name '*.log' 2>/dev/null | head -1) && [ -n "$f" ] && break; done`,
686	    `if [ -n "$f" ]; then echo "NXLOG:FILE:$f"; tail -n ${lines} "$f" 2>/dev/null; fi`,
687	  ].join("\n");
688	  const { stdout } = await exec(conn, script, QUICK_TIMEOUT_MS);
689	  const all = stdout.split(/\r?\n/);
690	  let unit: string | null = null;
691	  const out: string[] = [];
692	  for (const l of all) {

694	    if (m) {
695	      unit = m[1] === "none" ? null : m[1];
696	      continue;

698	    if (/^NXLOG:FILE:/.test(l)) continue;
699	    out.push(l);

770	  const raw = response.trim();
771	  if (family === "minecraft") {
772	    // Strip ANSI escape codes — Paper/Spigot embed color codes in RCON responses.
773	    const clean = raw.replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g, "");
774	    // Vanilla: "There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Alice, Bob"
775	    const m1 = /players online:\s*(.+)$/im.exec(clean);
776	    if (m1) {
777	      const names = m1[1].split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
778	      return { players: names.map((name) => ({ name })), raw };
779	    }
780	    // Paper: "There are 2 out of maximum 20 players online.\ndefault: Alice, Bob"
781	    const m2 = /players online\.\s*\n.*?:\s*(.+)$/im.exec(clean);
782	    if (m2) {
783	      const names = m2[1].split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
784	      return { players: names.map((name) => ({ name })), raw };
785	    }
786	    return { players: [], raw };
787	  }
788	  if (family === "palworld") {
789	    // "name,playeruid,steamid" lines, first line is a header.
790	    const lines = raw.split(/\r?\n/).map((l) => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
791	    const players: Player[] = [];
792	    for (const l of lines) {
793	      if (/^name\s*,/i.test(l)) continue;
794	      const cols = l.split(",");
795	      if (cols[0]) players.push({ name: cols[0].trim(), extra: cols.slice(1).join(",").trim() || undefined });

798	  }

3	 *
4	 * WHY THIS IS ITS OWN MODULE. Two independent things have to both be true, and
5	 * until now neither was checked before the button was drawn:
6	 *
7	 *   1. the worker knows WHERE this game keeps its mods
8	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `modDirShell`), and
9	 *   2. the worker can turn this entry's source into a DOWNLOAD URL
10	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `resolveUrl`).
11	 *
12	 * The catalogue is far wider than either. Expanding it from 124 entries across
13	 * five games to 491 across eight made that gap much bigger rather than smaller:
14	 * every Factorio, Satisfactory, Palworld, CS2 and V Rising entry got an Install
15	 * button that reaches the worker and comes back "Auto-install isn't wired for
16	 * this game yet." A button whose only outcome is an error is worse than no
17	 * button, and it is worse again at 178 of them.
18	 *
19	 * So the two lists live here, `worker/game-mods.ts` imports them rather than
20	 * keeping its own copies, and the panel asks the same question before it
21	 * decides what to render. One source of truth, so the UI and the worker cannot
22	 * disagree about what is possible.
23	 *
24	 * ADDING A FAMILY is deliberately a two-part job: add its directory to
25	 * `modDirShell` AND its slug here. Adding it here alone re-creates exactly the
26	 * failure this module exists to prevent.
27	 */

29	/** Families whose mod directory `worker/game-mods.ts` knows how to find. */
30	export const INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = new Set(["minecraft", "rust", "valheim"]);
31	
32	/** Sources `worker/game-mods.ts` can resolve to a downloadable file. */
33	export const RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = new Set(["modrinth", "spigotmc", "umod", "thunderstore"]);
34	
35	export type InstallSupport =
36	  | { ok: true }
37	  | { ok: false; reason: "family" | "source"; message: string };
38	
39	/**
40	 * Can this entry be installed for the customer, or does it have to be done by
41	 * hand? The message is customer-facing and says which of the two is missing,
42	 * because they lead to different next steps: a family we can't reach means
43	 * upload it yourself, a source we can't fetch from means download it first.
44	 */
45	export function installSupport(family: string, source: string): InstallSupport {
46	  if (!INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES.has(family)) {
47	    return {
48	      ok: false,
49	      reason: "family",
50	      message: "We can't place files for this game automatically yet — install it yourself in Files.",
51	    };
52	  }
53	  if (!RESOLVABLE_SOURCES.has(source)) {
54	    return {
55	      ok: false,
56	      reason: "source",
57	      message: "This source doesn't offer a direct download we can fetch — grab the file and upload it in Files.",
58	    };
59	  }
60	  return { ok: true };
61	}

## 8. Worker config-apply mechanism (`worker/game-config.ts`, 1424 lines)
- `gameConfigApply(job)` (line 132-245): resolves family/schema, computes `realApply = familyRealApplyEnabled(family)` (true only if `family ∈ REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` or `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG=1`). If not real and not `SANDBOX`, **throws** — settings are never silently faked in prod (line 167-173).
- **Real path dispatch** (`applyRealConfig`, line 435-454): a hardcoded `switch(family)` with cases only for `minecraft`, `rust`, `valheim`, `cs2`, `palworld`, `bedrock`. For everything else: `default: return { ok:false, notes:['No real apply implemented for "<family>".'] }`.
- **The actual write mechanism, for the two patterns that matter to you:**
  - **Env-var/container-recreate** (used by palworld, rust, valheim, bedrock — the pattern you'll extend for the other 10 Docker-run families): `readContainerEnv(conn, container)` reads `docker inspect <container> --format '{{json .Config.Env}}'` into a `Map` (line 534-551); mutate the map; `writeEnvFile(conn, sftp, path, envMap)` writes it to a root-only file like `/root/palworld.env` via SFTP + `chmod 600` (line 562-566); then `recreateGameContainer(conn, {family, container, runFlags, image})` (line 588-654) does the stop/rename/`docker create`/`systemctl start`/verify-alive/rollback dance through whichever systemd unit `resolveGameUnit()` (line 418-430) resolves from `controlSpec(family).serviceHints`. `applyPalworld` (line 1319-1354) is the concrete example: `PALWORLD_ENV_MAP` (line 1298-1317) maps schema field key → env var name + formatter, e.g. `pvp: { env: "IS_PVP", format: v => bool(v)==="true" ? "True":"False" }`.
  - **Key=value file rewrite** (used by minecraft): `updateKeyValue(content, updates)` (line 461-479) patches `key=value` lines in an existing file read via `sftpRead`/written via `sftpWrite`.
- **For your 10 non-palworld families, none of this exists yet** — you'll be writing new `apply<Family>` functions and adding cases to the `switch` in `applyRealConfig`, plus adding each family to `REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` in `lib/game-config.ts:1799` once verified.
